result.label: Scale Plastic Modeling
result.summary: In: 1/72 scale WWII aircraft kits, tools, techniques (building, painting, weathering), brands and manufacturers, and the hobby community. Out: other scales and subjects such as cars, ships, figures, or sci-fi, except where they overlap with the core.

children.label: Kits and Brands
children.summary: The injection-molded plastic aircraft kits and the manufacturers who produce them in 1/72 scale.

children.label: Core Hand Tools
children.summary: The basic cutters, knives, files and clamps that separate parts from sprues and clean up seams.

children.label: Glues and Cements
children.summary: The solvent cements and adhesives that fuse plastic parts into a single rigid airframe.

children.label: Paints and Finishes
children.summary: The acrylic, enamel and lacquer paints, primers and varnishes used to colour and protect the model.

children.label: Painting Techniques
children.summary: The methods of applying paint, from brushing and spraying to masking and camouflage patterns.

children.label: Weathering Techniques
children.summary: The methods of adding wear, grime, exhaust staining and chipping that make a model look used.

children.label: Decals and Markings
children.summary: The printed transfers and stencils that give the model its squadron codes, insignia and warning text.

children.label: Workspace and Safety
children.summary: The ventilation, lighting, storage and protective gear needed to work safely with solvents and paints.

children.label: Modeling Community
children.summary: The clubs, forums, shows, contests and online groups where modelers share skills, reference and kits.

children.label: Tamiya
children.summary: Japanese manufacturer known for accurate, easy-to-build styrene kits.

children.label: Hasegawa
children.summary: Japanese kit maker producing many WWII aircraft in 1/72 scale.

children.label: Airfix
children.summary: British brand that popularised plastic scale modeling since the 1950s.

children.label: Eduard
children.summary: Czech company making photo-etched details, masks and decals for models.

children.label: Special Hobby
children.summary: Czech manufacturer focused on obscure and niche WWII aircraft subjects.

children.label: Revell
children.summary: German manufacturer producing a wide range of beginner-friendly model kits.

children.label: Kit Scale Options
children.summary: Choosing between 1/72 and other scales for WWII aircraft models.

children.label: Aftermarket Accessories
children.summary: Third-party resin, decal and detail sets that upgrade standard kits.

branchLinks.why: Photo-etched and resin parts are usually attached with super glue.
Group builds often fix a subject or scale, such as 1/72 WWII aircraft.
